concept.name: Kubernetes
concept.title: Kubernetes, from image to cluster
concept.definition: Kubernetes runs your app across a group of computers, restarts it when something breaks, and scales it when traffic grows — so you do not babysit each machine.
concept.problem: Running an application on many machines by hand makes deployment, scaling, recovery, and networking fragile.

nodes.label: Container Image
nodes.caption: the recipe
nodes.description: A container image is the recipe: the files and settings needed to start the same build of the app on any computer.

nodes.label: You
nodes.caption: browser or phone
nodes.description: You are the person or device using the app — a browser, a phone, or another service.

nodes.label: The Manager
nodes.caption: places and heals
nodes.description: The Manager is part of the Control Plane. It places Pods, restarts crashes, and follows the written plan.

nodes.label: Written Plan
nodes.caption: desired state
nodes.description: The written plan is the desired state: what should be running, how many copies, and which image they use.

nodes.label: Service
nodes.caption: stable front desk
nodes.description: A Service is a stable front desk. You call one address; Kubernetes forwards work to healthy Pods behind it.

nodes.label: Pod A
nodes.caption: running copy 1
nodes.description: A Pod is the smallest unit Kubernetes will place. Pod A is one running copy of the app.

nodes.label: Pod B
nodes.caption: running copy 2
nodes.description: Pod B is a second running copy, giving spare capacity if one copy fails or traffic grows.

nodes.label: Container
nodes.caption: the packed app
nodes.description: A Container is one running copy of the image — the packed app itself inside Pod A.

nodes.label: Container
nodes.caption: the packed app
nodes.description: A Container is one running copy of the same image inside Pod B.

groups.label: Kubernetes Cluster — the campus
groups.description: The Cluster is the whole campus: Worker Nodes that run the app, plus a Control Plane that keeps the written plan and heals problems.

groups.label: Control Plane — the office
groups.description: The Control Plane is the office that decides where work goes and heals what breaks.

groups.label: Worker Node 1 — a computer
groups.description: A Worker Node is one computer that actually runs Pods.

groups.label: Worker Node 2 — a computer
groups.description: A Worker Node is one computer that actually runs Pods.

chapters.title: Docker packs the app
chapters.explanation: A container image is the recipe for the app. A Container is one running copy of that recipe, packed so it behaves the same on any computer.

chapters.title: A Pod holds the box
chapters.explanation: A Pod is the smallest box Kubernetes will place. It holds one or more Containers that should live and die together.

chapters.title: Worker Nodes are computers
chapters.explanation: A Worker Node is one computer in the cluster. Kubernetes places Pods onto these machines and can move them if a machine fails.

chapters.title: The Cluster is the campus
chapters.explanation: The Cluster is the whole campus: Worker Nodes that run the app, plus a Control Plane that keeps the written plan and heals problems.

chapters.title: How you reach the app
chapters.explanation: A Service is a stable front desk. You talk to one address; Kubernetes forwards the work to whichever Pods are healthy behind it.

contextCards.title: How the pieces nest
points: The image packs the app into a Container that runs the same everywhere.
A Pod holds that Container — the smallest unit Kubernetes will place.
A Worker Node is one computer; the Cluster is the whole campus plus the office.

contextCards.title: What the neighbors do
points: Control Plane: places Pods, restarts crashes, keeps the written plan.
Service: a stable front desk so you never hunt for a Pod.
Image is the recipe; a Container is one running copy of it.

contextCards.title: Why this exists
points: A computer fails: work moves to another Worker Node.
Traffic grows: more Pods start from the same image.
You keep calling one Service while Pods are replaced behind it.
